_comment: Notification-hook surface: every priority critical|high entry whose last_changed_at falls in the last 7 days, most recently changed first. last_changed_at = max(discovered_at, every non-internal updates[].at): it moves on a new finding AND on every reader-facing update, correction or improvement (updated_at moves only on a type:update record). Poll this file and alert on a new `id` OR a changed `last_changed_at` for a known id. `immediate_action` is non-null exactly when priority is critical. URLs are absolute (`url` == `permalink`; `markdown_url` is the entry's raw Markdown source). Schema: {id, url, permalink, markdown_url, priority, kind, headline, summary, discovered_at, updated_at|null, last_changed_at, updates[{at,type,summary}], immediate_action:{title,action}|null, actions[], exploited, kev, cve_ids[], cves[{id,cvss|null,status[],affected|null,fixed|null}], affected_products[], entities[], techniques[], tags[], sectors[], regions[], verification, classification|null, org_triage:{category,rationale}|null}. exploited = an exploitation tag or a CVE status of exploited/cisa-kev; kev = a CVE on the CISA KEV list. techniques[] carries the entry's MITRE ATT&CK ids (frontmatter + prose-derived, revoked ids resolved forward); classification is the collapsed Admiralty code (e.g. B2). For the do-now task list of every priority, poll data/actions.json. See docs/pipeline.md.

actions: Upgrade every PaperCut NG/MF Application Server, Site Server and secondary/print server to the security maintenance release for its line (26.0.5, 25.0.13 or 24.1.11, the v24 build the September bulletin now names), starting with any still on Emergency Patch Release 1 or 2, because the emergency builds do not carry the fix for CVE-2026-82077, an administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw that the vendor's September bulletin lists as fixed in 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10; for v23 and earlier, immediately restrict the Application Server's web interface to trusted/internal IP addresses only; no patch exists for that line. On every server, patched or not, set the advanced config key auth.webservices.auth-token to a long random secret and limit auth.webservices.allowed-addresses to the hosts that call the XML-RPC API, because Hunt.io says an instance hardened against the Tapestry bypass is not necessarily protected against the XML-RPC route it recovered, which works when the allowlist is too permissive or no token is set.

Before patching or restarting an internet-facing server, preserve the server/logs directory and process tree; check server.log for the two vendor-documented error strings and for an unexplained gap or truncation, check derby.log for a Derby boot line naming an in-memory database directory ending in "pwn", and hunt for a Windows service named "Remote Access Service" running SimpleService.exe (SimpleHelp) or an unexpected AnyDesk install, as PaperCut's own published incident data names both as an observed post-compromise access method.

Given GreyNoise's confirmed domain-admin escalation paths, verify no PaperCut Application Server is domain-joined with a privileged service account or hosted on a domain controller, and confirm domain controllers reachable from any PaperCut host are patched against the 2021 noPac flaws (CVE-2021-42278/CVE-2021-42287); GreyNoise reports the AI-orchestrated campaign reaching full domain admin through these paths in as little as five minutes after initial access.

alerts.headline: A pre-auth RCE chain in PaperCut NG/MF was exploited before any patch existed; tested maintenance releases now replace three emergency patches
alerts.summary: PaperCut NG and PaperCut MF (all versions) carry an unauthenticated remote-code-execution chain, CVE-2026-81578 (auth bypass, CVSS4.0 8.8) and CVE-2026-82078 (unsafe dynamic class loading, CVSS4.0 9.4), that PaperCut confirmed under active exploitation on 2026-08-27, before any CVE or patch existed. Fully tested maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10 (10 September 2026) replace the emergency patches and are the vendor's recommended build (the September bulletin, revised 2026-10-13, now names 24.1.11 for v24); servers still on Emergency Patch Release 1 or 2 need to upgrade now. There is no fix for v23 and earlier, and Huntress estimates 47% of the PaperCut installs it tracks run v23 or older. GreyNoise now documents an AI-agent-orchestrated mass-exploitation campaign against this same chain, compromising at least 440 instances across 395 identified organizations since 31 August 2026, reaching full domain admin in as little as five minutes via legacy Active Directory escalation paths. watchTowr's write-up of 2026-10-09 shows the 28 August emergency build could still be taken without authentication through the Setup Wizard forms, and names CVE-2026-82077, an administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw that the vendor lists as fixed in 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10. Hunt.io's recovery of the attacker's open directories (2026-10-15) adds a second route to code execution through PaperCut's XML-RPC API, usable when its address allowlist is too permissive or no explicit token is set, a cron-kept reverse SOCKS tunnel, and live pivots into 45 victims, with Switzerland among the countries listed.

updates.summary: PaperCut shipped Emergency Patch Release 3 on 1 September 2026, superseding Release 2 and fixing two regressions Release 2 had introduced (broken SAML login; lost legacy Microsoft SQL Server driver support for external card lookup). PaperCut also confirms a second, more sophisticated wave of attacks against still-unpatched, internet-facing servers, and separately published incident data naming a post-compromise chain installing a SimpleHelp remote-access service and AnyDesk for durable access.

GreyNoise documents an AI-agent-orchestrated mass-exploitation campaign against this chain beginning 31 August 2026, using hundreds of AI agents to opportunistically compromise 440 PaperCut instances across 395 organizations in 48 countries, reaching domain admin against 12 of them in as little as five minutes via LSASS credential harvesting, the 2021 noPac flaws, or a PaperCut host running on the domain controller itself, all finishing with a DCSync-based NTDS.DIT credential dump.

PaperCut published fully tested maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10 on 10 September 2026. They carry every fix from the three emergency patches plus further hardening, and replace the emergency patches as the recommended build. A server on Emergency Patch Release 3 is protected and can schedule the move normally; one on Release 1 or 2 should upgrade now. There is still no fix for v23 and earlier. PaperCut also reports that new compromises slowed considerably in early September while unpatched, exposed servers are still targeted. CISA added both CVEs to its KEV catalog on 2026-08-31, which the status fields now record.

watchTowr published on 2026-10-09 how the emergency patches were bypassed in turn: the 28 August emergency build could still be taken without authentication through the Setup Wizard forms, and a new administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw, CVE-2026-82077, is fixed only in 26.0.5 and 25.0.13, not in the emergency builds. No source names exploitation of either, though PaperCut says Emergency Patch Release 3 closes off further attack vectors it has seen exploited. Earlier statements the cited sources do not support were corrected where they stood: the 2023 precedent, the university-customer statement, the emergency-patch chronology and the detection wording.

Hunt.io recovered the attacker's open directories (2026-10-15) and reports a second route to code execution through PaperCut's XML-RPC API that does not use the Tapestry bypass and works when the API allowlist is too permissive or no explicit token is set, a cron-kept reverse SOCKS tunnel, an offline LSA-secret playbook and 45 victims with live internal pivots, Switzerland among the countries listed. Hunt.io does not report the XML-RPC route used against a victim; PaperCut's documentation names the token and allowlist settings that close it. PaperCut's September bulletin, revised 2026-10-13, now lists CVE-2026-82077 as fixed in 24.1.10 and names 24.1.11 as the v24 build.

actions: Upgrade every Ivanti Connect Secure appliance on 25.1.1.1 or earlier, 25.1.2.2 or earlier, or 22.8R2.4 or earlier to 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.1 or 22.8R2.5 now, internet-facing appliances first; 22.7.x and below are not affected.

Run a compromise check on every appliance that was reachable on an affected build, starting with proxy, load balancer or WAF logs back to at least 2026-10-03 for welcome.cgi requests that carry an X-DSCGI-PATH header; where compromise cannot be excluded, first cut the appliance off from the internet and the internal network and snapshot a virtual appliance's file system and memory without powering it down, then follow Ivanti's recovery steps and reset the domain service account, LAPS and local passwords, certificates, API keys, the Kerberos tickets of its service accounts and the licence-server authentication the appliance held, because CERT-FR knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets.

alerts.headline: Exploited Ivanti Connect Secure chain: its root step had no fix at disclosure, and it evades the Integrity Checker

immediate_action.action: Ivanti and CISA confirm exploitation of CVE-2026-104935, and Volexity saw the chain used against a fully patched 22.8R2.4 appliance from 2026-10-03. Upgrade every Connect Secure appliance on 25.1.1.1 or earlier, 25.1.2.2 or earlier, or 22.8R2.4 or earlier to 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.1 or 22.8R2.5, internet-facing ones first. Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool cannot see this chain and the root-escalation step had no fix when Volexity reported, so an appliance that was reachable on an affected build needs a compromise check and rotation of the Active Directory service account, LAPS passwords and other secrets it could reach.
immediate_action.title: Patch Ivanti Connect Secure now, then check the appliance and its AD account for compromise

alerts.summary: Ivanti disclosed CVE-2026-104935 on 2026-10-13, an authentication bypass in Connect Secure that lets a remote unauthenticated attacker run commands, and says it is aware of limited exploitation; CISA listed it in KEV the same day. Volexity found a cluster it calls UTA0576 chaining it with a root escalation that Ivanti had not fixed when Volexity reported (a separate record, CVE-2026-111357, now covers that step), patching library code in memory only so Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool sees no file change, and going after the appliance's Active Directory service account, LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys. Fixed builds are 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.1 and 22.8R2.5 (Rapid7 also lists 25.1.3.0, which CERT-FR counts as affected); a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and CERT-FR says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance and tells owners to isolate and preserve it before any reset.

updates.summary: CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-14 says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance, and sets the response order: isolate the appliance from the internet and the internal network, snapshot and keep it powered on, then analyse before any reset; its rotation scope also covers Kerberos tickets of the service accounts and licence-server authentication. CERT-FR also counts 25.1.3.0 as affected, so the fixed-build targets now name 25.1.3.1.

The unfixed root-escalation step of the chain now has its own identifier, CVE-2026-111357, published 2026-10-15, and the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates it is exploited in the wild; its description names only 22.8R2.4 as affected, says the step was exploited in the wild in October 2026 and states no fixed build, so scanners, SIEM enrichment and tickets can now follow the step by ID.

actions: Upgrade every Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center installation to a fixed version of its line (Bitbucket 9.4.26, 10.2.8 or 10.5.1; Confluence 9.2.26 or 10.2.19; Jira Service Management 5.12.40, 10.3.26 or 11.3.12; Jira Software 9.12.40, 10.3.26 or 11.3.12; Bamboo 10.2.24 or 12.1.12; Crowd 6.3.7, 7.0.3, 7.1.7 or 7.2.4) and Crucible and Fisheye to 4.9.15, internet-reachable instances first; until each is upgraded, take it off the internet or put Atlassian's web application firewall or Tomcat rewrite rule in front of it.

Confirm that every vulnerability scanner, SIEM enrichment rule and ticket keyed on CVE-2026-21589 still reports each affected Atlassian instance as open; where the rejected ID has dropped it, track the flaw by Atlassian's advisory and the fixed versions above until a replacement ID appears.

alerts.headline: Atlassian's CVE-2026-21589 record was rejected on 16 October, but the flaw, its fixes and its exploitation stand
alerts.summary: Atlassian's advisory of 2026-10-05 fixes CVE-2026-21589, an unauthenticated arbitrary file access flaw in every version of Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center, plus Crucible and Fisheye (CVSS 4.0 9.3), and tells customers to patch immediately or take internet-facing instances off the internet. watchTowr Labs published the root cause, the request shape and a runnable checker on 2026-10-06, and exploitation attempts followed the same day: Previdian's honeypot sensors recorded attempts from dozens of addresses in about twenty countries, SANS ISC recorded similar attempts on its own honeypots, and a Nuclei template exists; neither honeypot operator reports a compromise. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-15 on evidence of active exploitation, without saying what the evidence is. Where Jira is integrated with Crowd, the file read exposes a plaintext Crowd application password that gives access to Crowd as an administrator of that application. The CVE record for this ID was marked rejected on 2026-10-16 with only a generic reason, while Atlassian's advisory and fixed versions are unchanged, so tooling keyed on the ID can lose track of an exploited flaw.

updates.summary: watchTowr Labs published the root cause (a path-separator substitution in the web-resource library shared by Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket), the request shape and a runnable checker on 2026-10-06, and shows that where Jira is integrated with Crowd the file read exposes a plaintext Crowd application password that gives administrator access to Crowd for that application. The flaw moves from a patch-now issue with unpublished mechanics to one with public mechanics and a Crowd credential to rotate; no exploitation is reported. Atlassian's Crowd ticket lists the same fixed builds as the advisory.

Exploitation attempts began on 2026-10-06, the day watchTowr published its write-up and proof of concept: Previdian's sensors have recorded at least 129 attempts from at least 22 addresses in eight countries, SANS ISC recorded similar attempts against Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket on its own honeypots, all from one cloud provider, and a Nuclei template exists; the Canadian Cyber Centre's bulletin now cites open-source reporting of in-the-wild exploitation. The status moves from patch-available to exploited, with no compromise reported and the flaw not listed in CISA's KEV catalog on Previdian's page.

CISA added CVE-2026-21589 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-15 on evidence of active exploitation, which moves the flaw from honeypot-observed attempts to government-confirmed exploitation; CISA names neither the evidence, the actor nor any victim, and neither CISA nor the honeypot operators report a compromise; Previdian's honeypot count has grown to 607 attempts from 65 addresses in 20 countries, and NCSC Switzerland has listed the flaw as actively exploited since 2026-10-12.

Atlassian, the assigner, rejected the CVE record for CVE-2026-21589 on 2026-10-16, giving only the generic reason that its publication may have been a false positive or a mistake; ENISA's EUVD record mirrors it and still lists exploitation since 2026-10-15. Atlassian's advisory still uses the ID with the same fixed versions, and no source says why the record was rejected or whether a replacement ID will follow, so tooling keyed on the ID can lose track of an exploited flaw.

actions: Inventory every Windows host that runs AOMEI Backupper or AnyViewer and check each for scheduled tasks named RadminComponentRuntime or NitroRuntime, a Radmin directory under the user's local application data and cached update files in the install tree's Tmphtml folder, searching proxy and firewall logs back to April 2026; isolate any host that matches and keep the cached files before any cleanup.
alerts.headline: GTIG: AOMEI update files were altered for minutes at a time to push a backdoor; Switzerland among victim countries
alerts.summary: Google's GTIG and ManageEngine's METAL report that a cluster tracked as UNC7017 altered two configuration files on AOMEI's update servers for five to ten minutes at a time between April and July 2026, so any Backupper or AnyViewer client that polled during a window downloaded and ran the CROSSROAD downloader, which installed the SHINYROAD backdoor beside a signed Radmin binary. No software flaw is involved, GTIG names Switzerland among 11 victim countries, and the vendor's server-side repair does not clean a host that already ran the downloader, so installations need an endpoint hunt covering April to July 2026.

alerts.headline: Drupal patches a critical Field UI RCE reachable through contributed modules; uninstall field_ui if you cannot update
alerts.summary: Drupal's advisory SA-CORE-2026-014 of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-108097, a remote code execution flaw in the core Field UI module rated Critical (19 of 25): core alone is not directly exploitable, but several exploit paths exist through contributed modules and at least one known path needs no login. Fixed releases are 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19; 11.2.x and below, 10.5.x and below and Drupal 8 and 9 get no fix, and until a site is updated the advisory's mitigation is to uninstall the Field UI module. The advisory records no public exploit at publication, and The Hacker News relays the Security Team's pre-announcement warning that exploits might be developed within hours or days.

actions: Apply the BT26-05-RS patch to every self-hosted BeyondTrust Remote Support appliance now and confirm in the /appliance interface that it is installed (a build older than 24.3.1 must be upgraded first, which closes the hole but does not undo earlier exposure); apply it to self-hosted Privileged Remote Access appliances too, which BeyondTrust patched as a precaution.

For every appliance that was internet-reachable on a build up to 26.2.3 at any time since late August 2026: before any change, snapshot a virtual appliance with memory and export its disk, and collect the off-box syslog, reverse-proxy or WAF and perimeter firewall logs because the actor deletes on-appliance logs; then redeploy from a clean, fully patched image every appliance whose compromise status is confirmed or unknown, and rotate the credentials it held in dependency order, including the Remote Support Vault and any credential typed into a support session.

cves.affected: Remote Support, all versions up to 26.2.3 (self-hosted; SaaS tenants were patched by 2026-10-09)
cves.fixed: BT26-05-RS patch for versions 24.3.1 to 26.2.3; versions older than 24.3.1 must first be upgraded to a supported release

alerts.headline: BeyondTrust patches an exploited Remote Support zero-day; the actor's persistence survives reboot and reset

immediate_action.action: BeyondTrust and Google's Threat Intelligence Group confirm that an unauthenticated flaw in Remote Support (all versions up to 26.2.3) was exploited as a zero-day from late August 2026, GTIG attributing it to a suspected China-nexus espionage actor, and GTIG warns organizations to prepare for widespread exploitation now that the flaw is public. Apply the BT26-05-RS patch to every self-hosted appliance (builds older than 24.3.1 must be upgraded first). The actor's persistence survives reboot and configuration reset and it deletes on-appliance logs, so snapshot and collect off-box logs from any appliance that was internet-reachable on an affected build, then redeploy from a clean patched image any whose compromise status is confirmed or unknown and rotate everything it held.
immediate_action.title: Patch BeyondTrust Remote Support now, review every appliance exposed since late August and rebuild any with confirmed or unknown compromise status

alerts.summary: BeyondTrust's advisory BT26-05 of 2026-10-15 fixes CVE-2026-102764, an improper origin validation in an internal messaging component of Remote Support that lets a remote attacker perform file operations on the appliance without authenticating; all versions up to 26.2.3 are affected. Google's Threat Intelligence Group found ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploiting it as a zero-day in late August 2026, leaving a web shell, a root-SUID shell and a sudoers entry that survive reboot and configuration reset, so a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and a rebuild where its status is confirmed or unknown.

actions: Find every AhsayCBS server your organisation or your managed-service suppliers run, including those already on v10.3.4.0 or v9.15.2.59, and apply the hotfix v10.3.4.45 (v10) or v9.15.2.70 (v7, v8, v9) now, then reboot it; the hotfixes sit behind Ahsay's partner portal, so ask the integrator or Ahsay for the build, and until it is applied keep the management web interface behind a VPN or an allowlist of trusted addresses.

Compromise-check every AhsayCBS server that was internet-reachable since 2026-10-04 against the indicators Huntress and Bitdefender publish, an OpenSSH service nobody installed included, and re-image any host with a confirmed compromise from a trusted backup, because the hotfix does not remove a webshell or a persistence mechanism that is already there.

alerts.headline: Ahsay admits its earlier AhsayCBS patches were incomplete; the hotfixes are partner-only and CISA lists both flaws as exploited
alerts.summary: Huntress observed from 2026-10-07 23:20 UTC attackers chaining two AhsayCBS flaws, CVE-2026-105133 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-105134 (code execution as SYSTEM through the Replication Receiver API), against internet-exposed servers of the backup management console that managed service providers and system integrators mainly use, dropping JSP webshells and an XMRig cryptominer; Bitdefender MDR investigated three intrusions through the same chain, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14. Ahsay now says its earlier patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully address the flaws, so servers on them are still exposed; the fixes are the hotfixes v10.3.4.45 (v10) and v9.15.2.70 (v7, v8 and v9), available only to partners with a portal login, and a server that was reachable before the hotfix needs a compromise check.

updates.summary: Ahsay says its previous patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully fix the flaws and names the hotfixes v10.3.4.45 and v9.15.2.70, available only to partners; Huntress verified the v10 hotfix, CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14, and Bitdefender MDR describes three intrusions through the chain. Hotfixes now cover v10 and v7 to v9, through the partner portal.

actions: Restrict the management interface of every PA-Series, VM-Series and Panorama to a jump box or trusted internal addresses now, then upgrade each to the fixed build of its train (11.2.14 and 11.2.15 units to 11.2.16, published 2026-10-15); there is no workaround.

On every device whose management interface was reachable from untrusted networks, search management-interface logins, administrator-change records and upstream firewall logs for the three source addresses Palo Alto lists in the advisory's FAQ, and treat a match as a root compromise.

alerts.headline: Palo Alto confirms limited exploitation of a PAN-OS management-interface root flaw; no workaround, 11.2.16 now published
alerts.summary: Palo Alto Networks' advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-0322, a code injection in the PAN-OS management interface that lets an authenticated attacker with network access run code as root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama; the advisory is tagged as attacked and reports very limited exploitation, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. There is no workaround and the risk is highest where the management interface is reachable from the internet; 11.2.16, the fixed build for units on 11.2.14 and 11.2.15, was published on 2026-10-15, so every train now has a fixed build.

updates.summary: Palo Alto Networks published PAN-OS 11.2.16 on 2026-10-15, the fixed build for units on 11.2.14 and 11.2.15 that had none when the advisory appeared; every supported train now has a fixed build, exploitation is unchanged at very limited, and there is still no workaround.

actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.
alerts.headline: CERT-FR adds Copeland and Dixell xweb to the hijacked refrigeration controllers; NCSC.ch rates the attacks exploited
alerts.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, which BFMTV reports as a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of stores. CERT-FR's alert, revised on 2026-10-13, reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and now also of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, says campaigns are probably still running and that a factory reset alone does not protect an unpatched end-of-life unit, and NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited. Danfoss says most affected units are legacy products or current AK-SM800A units on outdated firmware; no source names an actor, the flaw or how the attackers got in, and the Paris prosecutor is investigating.

updates.summary: CERT-FR revised its alert on 2026-10-13 to add Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb to the compromised controllers, says campaigns are probably still running, and says a factory reset alone is insufficient on an unpatched end-of-life unit. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory rating the activity actively exploited and naming the current AK-SM 800A on outdated firmware, and Danfoss says that is the case for the affected current units. Blick reports that Migros uses the same Danfoss systems in a limited number of Swiss stores and sees no sign they were targeted.

Censys's exposure report of 2026-10-14 points to three published 2025 AK-SM 800A flaws that Danfoss patched more than a year earlier and gives their firmware boundaries (4.3.1 or later fixes all three; Danfoss has not confirmed the vector), and shows exposed French controllers falling about 71 percent in three days with patched and unpatched builds leaving at the same rate, which Censys reads as operators taking units offline rather than patching.

actions: Update the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app (richdocumentscode) to 26.4.303 or remove it on every Nextcloud server that runs it; disabling the app does not stop the request, and on Nextcloud 29 or older, which is end of life, upgrade Nextcloud or remove the app.

On each such server, search the web access logs back to at least early September 2026 for requests to apps/richdocumentscode/proxy.php that carry $( or an encoded .. in the path, and the app directory for PHP files that are not part of the release; on a hit, treat every secret the web server account can read as exposed and rotate it.

alerts.headline: Exploited Nextcloud Collabora CODE app flaw: disabling the app does not help; update to 26.4.303 or remove it
alerts.summary: CVE-2026-110447 is an OS command injection in proxy.php of the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server, the richdocumentscode app that runs Collabora inside Nextcloud; versions before 26.4.303 are affected, the GitHub advisory record says it was exploited in the wild in September and October 2026, and a hoster reported web shells on its Nextcloud servers on 2026-09-11. Disabling the app does not stop the request, so it must be updated to 26.4.303 or removed; standalone Collabora Online servers are not affected.

actions: Run contentscannerstatus on every Cisco Secure Email Gateway that has File Reputation enabled in a mail policy and update Content Scanner Tools to 25.3.0.5525 or later with contentscannerupdate wherever automatic updates are off; the update needs no restart.

On every such gateway, and on each member of a cluster, run grep "System Security" system_logs now: on a suspected-compromise message keep the forensic data before upgrading, then follow Cisco's recovery steps (a new virtual machine on a fixed release with a fresh configuration and renewed credentials for a virtual appliance, Cisco TAC for a physical one) for every member of that cluster.

alerts.headline: Cisco's mail gateway has a second exploited root flaw in four weeks; the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update

immediate_action.action: An unauthenticated attacker who sends one crafted attachment through a gateway with File Reputation enabled gets root, Cisco confirms exploitation, and no workaround exists. Update Content Scanner Tools (no restart) on every gateway that has automatic updates disabled, then check system_logs on every cluster member for Cisco's "System Security" messages; Cisco strongly recommends restoring a compromised appliance and every member of its cluster, because the cluster's SSH private keys could be accessed.
immediate_action.title: Verify Content Scanner Tools 25.3.0.5525 or later on every Cisco Secure Email Gateway and run Cisco's compromise check today

alerts.summary: Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-76519, a relative path traversal in the Advanced Malware Protection (file reputation) path of Cisco Secure Email Gateway that lets an unauthenticated attacker who sends one crafted attachment through the device write files and run commands as root (CVSS 9.8); Cisco says its PSIRT became aware of exploitation in October 2026, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. Only gateways with File Reputation enabled on a mail policy and Content Scanner Tools earlier than 25.3.0.5525 are exposed; there is no workaround, and the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update that needs no restart or upgrade, and in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780.

alerts.headline: An attacker can reconstruct admin credentials for an exposed refrigeration controller offline, then silently disable cooling while the display reports normal
alerts.summary: Claroty Team82 disclosed 23 vulnerabilities (21 high) in Copeland XWEB300D/500D/500B PRO supervisory refrigeration controllers. Three chain to unauthenticated root RCE: an auth-bypass logic flaw in the Lua authentication handler, a deterministic admin-password generator derivable offline from the device's MAC address and current date, and an unauthenticated OS command injection via the libraries installation route. 17 further, authenticated-only command-injection flaws are individually CVE-mapped by the source at CVSS 8.0 each. Copeland fixed all 23 in firmware v1.13; no source read reports exploitation of these flaws, but CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-13 now reports numerous compromises of Copeland xweb refrigeration controllers without naming models, flaws or the entry vector.

updates.summary: This entry stated that CVE-2026-21718 is the deterministic admin-password flaw. Claroty does not say that. Its per-CVE table text for that identifier is generic ("an authentication bypass vulnerability... enabling any attackers to bypass the authentication requirement and achieve pre-authenticated code execution", CVSS v3 10.0), and the narrative section that describes the MAC-address-and-date key derivation names no CVE id at all. The binding was an inference by elimination rather than a stated attribution, and a defender tracing the identifier to a patch note would have been misled. The mechanism description stands as reported; the id binding is removed from the title-adjacent claim, the CVE record's affected text, the body and the action, and the sourcing note now states what Claroty does and does not attribute.

CERT-FR revised its refrigeration-controller alert on 2026-10-13 to say it knows of numerous compromises of Copeland xweb controllers, in addition to Danfoss and Dixell units; it names no models, flaws or entry vector, so the earlier 'no exploitation reported' no longer describes the product family.

actions: Upgrade every self-managed GitLab CE and EE instance on 19.2, 19.3 or 19.4 to 19.2.8, 19.3.5 or 19.4.2 now, internet-reachable instances and instances that allow open sign-up or public projects first, because a public proof of concept exists; 19.4.1 and 19.3.4 remain affected, and until each instance is upgraded, restrict anonymous access to public projects and stop untrusted users from creating or writing to public projects, which reduces exposure only to the path Rapid7 demonstrated.

cves.affected: self-managed GitLab CE/EE: 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, 19.4 before 19.4.2; GitLab rates it as needing no privileges, while the path Rapid7 demonstrated needs push access to a public project

alerts.headline: GitLab's CVSS 10.0 CI regex flaw now has a public PoC; the demonstrated path needs push access to a public project
alerts.summary: GitLab's critical patch release of 2026-10-12 fixes CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 3.1 10.0), an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler that lets code run on the server as the git user through a crafted expression in a CI/CD configuration; Rapid7 reported on 2026-10-13 that it reproduced it on 19.4.1 and published a proof of concept, and reports no confirmed exploitation in the wild. The demonstrated path needs push access to a public project (an ordinary account where users may create public projects), followed by a request to the CI lint API that carries no credentials. Self-managed CE and EE from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5 and 19.4 before 19.4.2 are affected, and NCSC Switzerland and CERT-EU both published advisories on 2026-10-12.

updates.summary: Rapid7 reported on 2026-10-13 that it reproduced arbitrary code execution on GitLab CE 19.4.1, published a proof of concept, and found no confirmed exploitation in the wild. The demonstrated path needs push access to a public project and then an unauthenticated CI lint request, so instances with open sign-up or public projects that untrusted users can write to are the exposed case.

alerts.headline: Microsoft patches an exploited Windows Shell zero-day that evades Mark of the Web protections on files and links
alerts.summary: Microsoft's 2026-10-13 updates fix CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell flaw that lets an attacker evade Mark of the Web defenses once a user opens a crafted file or link sent by email or instant message, so Windows does not show the dialog the tag normally triggers. Microsoft marks it exploited and CISA added it to KEV the same day; no source names the actor, the payload or the victims. Rapid7 says Windows Server 2012 gets no patch, while Microsoft lists fixes for Server 2012 R2 and every later supported release.

actions: Install SonicWall's platform hotfix 12.4.3-03670 or 12.5.0-03082 (or higher) on every SMA1000 6210, 7210 and 8200v, internet-reachable appliances first and including appliances already on the 12.4.3-03526 or 12.5.0-02952 hotfix from September; the appliance restarts when the installation finishes and no workaround is listed.

On every SMA1000 whose Work Place interface was internet-reachable before the hotfix, check its web access log back to 2026-10-06, the day the advisory was published, for the requests Previdian describes and, on a hit, run the compromise check SonicWall's earlier guidance describes.
alerts.headline: NCSC.ch now rates the SonicWall SMA1000 pre-auth SSRF actively exploited; SonicWall still reports no evidence
alerts.summary: SonicWall's advisory SNWLID-2026-0017 (2026-10-06) fixes four SMA1000 flaws, led by CVE-2026-102255, a pre-authentication server-side request forgery in the Work Place interface (CVSS 3.0 10.0) that affects 12.4.3-03526 and 12.5.0-02952, the hotfixes issued for the September zero-days; fixed builds are 12.4.3-03670 and 12.5.0-03082. Two honeypot operators report exploitation attempts against the flaw, Defused from 2026-10-08 and Previdian from 2026-10-09, and NCSC Switzerland recorded it as actively exploited on 2026-10-12, without anyone establishing that an attempt would have compromised a system; SonicWall's advisory still says it has no evidence of exploitation. The two earlier unauthenticated Work Place SSRF flaws this year were exploited, each paired with an administrator-only command-execution flaw.

updates.summary: Previdian, a honeypot operator, reported exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-102255 on 2026-10-09, three days after the patch: crafted OPTIONS requests to the Work Place interface that try to reach the appliance's internal CouchDB service. Previdian has not established whether any attempt would have compromised a system, and SonicWall's advisory still says it has no evidence of exploitation.

NCSC Switzerland edited its advisory on 2026-10-12 to record the flaw as actively exploited, citing two honeypot operators: Defused, which saw attempts against its decoys from 2026-10-08, and Previdian, from 2026-10-09 (135 attempts from two US addresses). Previdian has not established that an attempt would have compromised a system, and SonicWall's advisory still says it has no evidence of exploitation.

actions: Audit every npm publish token your organisation and its maintainers hold and revoke any that can publish without two-factor authentication, that exact token property, not package popularity, is what decides whether the worm spreads from a compromised developer to your packages.

On any developer workstation or build agent that installed a package from the keyv family since 2026-08-04, or tensorlake@0.5.144 since 2026-10-08, treat the AI-assistant, cloud, GitHub, Vault, SSH and Kubernetes credentials present on that host as disclosed and rotate them; the collector sweeps over 300 credential patterns in one pass, so partial rotation leaves the operator a working set. Isolate the host before revoking its GitHub token, because OX Security reports a switch that wipes the machine when the token is revoked; on a host that ran tensorlake@0.5.144, Socket and OX Security also name the gh-token-monitor persistence (a systemd user unit on Linux, a LaunchAgent on macOS, a scheduled task on Windows), which has to be removed before the token is revoked.

Stop treating a valid npm provenance attestation as evidence a package is clean; where release pipelines gate on provenance, change the check to pin on the workflow identity inside the Fulcio certificate and the Rekor log index, which is what Unit 42 says still discriminates.
alerts.headline: A self-propagating npm worm reaches packages totalling 1.3 billion monthly downloads, and its C2 address lives on-chain
alerts.summary: Elastic Security Labs identified CHAINDROP on 2026-08-04, a new wave of the Shai-Hulud npm worm that began with the compromise of the keyv maintainer and has backdoored over 400 npm packages whose combined reach Elastic puts at more than 1.3 billion monthly downloads, keyv alone at over 600 million. Execution comes from a package.json preinstall hook that downloads the Bun runtime to run an obfuscated 711 KB payload, which harvests over 300 credential patterns (AI-assistant tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure/Alibaba credentials, GitHub tokens, Vault tokens, SSH keys and Kubernetes service-account tokens) and self-propagates only when it finds an npm token that both carries package-write permission and can publish without two-factor authentication. Rather than hardcoding a command-and-control domain, CHAINDROP queries an Ethereum smart contract at runtime to resolve where to send the stolen material, so the operator rotates infrastructure without shipping a new payload. On 2026-10-08 a release of the tensorlake npm SDK carried the same payload family with valid build provenance, and Socket and OX Security describe a dead-man switch that wipes the owner's home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked before its persistence is removed.

updates.summary: Unit 42's analysis of CHAINDROP, the Shai-Hulud npm worm wave covered here on 2026-08-06, adds two mechanics that break controls defenders currently rely on. An embedded Python helper opens /proc/<pid>/maps and /proc/<pid>/mem on the GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process and searches live memory for OIDC tokens and runner secrets, so scanning files and environment variables at rest does not see it. A second, single-target path trades a runner OIDC token at npm's trusted-publishing endpoint for a real publish credential, injects a typosquatted dependency without touching install scripts, and then signs the result through Fulcio and Rekor, producing provenance Unit 42 is explicit is not forged.

A further package, tensorlake@0.5.144 (the npm SDK of an AI-agent sandbox platform), was published on 2026-10-08 with a Shai-Hulud-family payload through the project's normal GitHub Actions pipeline with valid build provenance; Socket and OX Security describe the dead-man switch that wipes the owner's home directory when the stolen GitHub token is revoked, and both say to remove its persistence before revoking. Socket matches the release to this wave, while OX Security says new keys may point to an independent actor reusing the name.
